question.text: Will any North American country have a CDC travel advisory issued in November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if a country in North America has a Travel Health Notice (THN) by the Centers for Disease Control at its [THN](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices) page newly issued in November 2026.
question.fine_print: No other resolution source will be used in resolving this question.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-31 (fetched): The CDC Travel Health Notices page was last reviewed 2026-10-19. These are its notices for specific North American countries:
  - Hepatitis A in Costa Rica: Level 1, **New**, 2026-09-18
  - Chikungunya in Nicaragua: Level 2, Updated, 2026-09-03
  - Chikungunya in Costa Rica: Level 2, Updated, 2026-07-30
  - Diphtheria in Haiti: Level 1, New, 2026-06-25
  - Hepatitis A in Canada (Manitoba): Level 1, New, 2026-06-04
  - Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever in Mexico: Level 1, 2025-12-23
  
  [CDC THN](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices)
- Some multi-country notices also cover North American countries: Global Dengue (Updated 2026-10-02, includes Cuba and Costa Rica) and Global Measles (2025-05-28). If one of these is updated, it is unclear whether that counts. The question says "newly issued", and the page marks status as "New" or "Updated". Nothing in October was new for a North American country. The newest notices on the page were Kenya Ebola (New, 10-19) and Ghana yellow fever (New, 10-16). [CDC THN](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet, because November has not started. The most recent new North American notice is still Costa Rica Hepatitis A from 2026-09-18, which matches the question background.
- 2026-10-30: The news items about a "CDC health declaration" for Guatemala and other travelers are about an Ebola/DRC attestation order for anyone flying into the US, effective 2026-11-03. That order is not a Travel Health Notice for a North American country, so it does not count. [Prensa Libre](https://www.prensalibre.com/guatemala/comunitario/nuevo-formulario-para-viajar-a-estados-unidos-tres-puntos-clave-sobre-su-vigencia-presentacion-fisica-o-digital-y-que-pasa-si-no-lo-lleva/), [rustourismnews](https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/10/30/new-us-flight-rule-from-november-3-now-applies-to-all-passengers-and-crew/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-28: A report says the CDC is keeping its Level 2 chikungunya notice for Costa Rica in place. [search summary; see Tico Times](https://ticotimes.net/2026/07/31/cdc-costa-rica-chikungunya-travel-notice-update)
- 2026-10-23: PAHO data show 58,549 suspected dengue cases in Mexico through epidemiological week 39. As of 2026-10-07, the CDC places Cuba in its high dengue transmission category. [CDC dengue areas](https://www.cdc.gov/dengue/areas-with-risk/index.html)
- 2026-10-22: A secondary source reports a PAHO alert dated 2026-10-16 that New World screwworm is spreading. It cites 592 human cases in Mexico by late September (117 in all of 2025), 295 in Guatemala and 302 in Honduras. I have not checked these numbers against PAHO directly. [MyVetCandy](https://www.myvetcandy.com/news/2026/10/22/flesh-eating-parasite-spreads-across-the-americas-as-human-cases-surge-and-veterinarians-face-a-growing-crisis)
- 2026-10-13: Canada issued its own Level 2 chikungunya notice, which covers Cuba and Nicaragua. That is a Canadian notice, not a CDC one. (search summary)
- 2026-08-03/04: The CDC issued a chikungunya notice for Nicaragua. Reports disagree on whether it started at Level 1 or Level 2. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322990/20260804/cdc-issues-nicaragua-chikungunya-alert-suspended-vaccine-leaves-us-travelers-one-choice.htm)
- About 2026-07-16 to 07-21: The CDC issued a chikungunya notice for Costa Rica, which later became Level 2 and was updated 07-30. [Tico Times](https://ticotimes.net/2026/07/31/cdc-costa-rica-chikungunya-travel-notice-update), [iHeart](https://www.iheart.com/content/2026-07-21-cdc-issues-travel-warning-after-outbreak-of-deadly-incurable-mosquito-virus/)

## 4. Base rates
I counted new CDC notices for specific North American countries that I could identify:
- About 2025-09: Chikungunya in Cuba, Level 2. That notice no longer appears on the THN page. [mesvaccins](https://www.mesvaccins.net/web/news/23483-les-cdc-emettent-une-alerte-aux-voyageurs-concernant-le-risque-de-chikungunya-a-cuba), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/us/cdc-warns-americans-traveling-4-countries-outbreak-untreatable-mosquito-disease.amp)
- 2025-12-23: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever in Mexico. The page shows no status label, so it may have been new or updated.
- 2026-06-04: Canada, Hepatitis A.
- 2026-06-25: Haiti, diphtheria.
- About 2026-07-16: Costa Rica, chikungunya.
- 2026-08-03: Nicaragua, chikungunya.
- 2026-09-18: Costa Rica, Hepatitis A.

That gives roughly 5 new notices in the 5 months from June to October 2026. June through September each had at least one, and October had none. Over the last 12 months there were about 6 to 7, spread across roughly 5 to 6 distinct months. I could not check January to May 2026 thoroughly, and I found no new North American notices in that period. If the months are treated as independent, a crude monthly rate is about 40 to 55%. Arbovirus notices bunch together in the rainy season, from mid-year to autumn.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets matches this question. They cover State Department advisories, Taiwan, oil, gold and similar topics. I found no Metaculus or Manifold question on CDC THNs for North America.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (Nov 1 to 30, 2026)
- Possible new notices:
  - Dengue or chikungunya spreading in Mexico, Cuba or Central America, where Canada already has a Cuba chikungunya notice that the CDC has not matched.
  - New World screwworm spreading in Mexico and Central America. The CDC has not issued THNs for screwworm before, as far as I found.
  - Oropouche.
  - Disease after the hurricane season in the Caribbean.
- If the Costa Rica, Nicaragua or Global Dengue notices are updated, that would probably show as "Updated" rather than "New", so it likely would not count.
- The CDC's focus on Ebola, including the attestation order from Nov 3, may take up THN staff time. That is my speculation, not something a source states.

Sources: the URLs linked inline above.

  - The newest notices on the page for any country are Kenya Ebola (New, Oct 19) and Ghana yellow fever (New, Oct 16). [CDC THN](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices)
- The page shows only one date per notice, labeled "New" or "Updated." It is unclear whether an "Updated" notice, a level change, or a country added to a multi-country notice (Global Dengue, Global Measles) would count as "newly issued." The question wording points to "New" only.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. No new North American notice appeared between Sep 18 and Oct 31, 2026.
- 2026-10-22, 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-30: CDC issued an Ebola order, then modified and expanded it. From Nov 3 it requires every air traveler to the US, including travelers from Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico, to attest they have not been in DR Congo. This is an entry requirement, not a THN for a North American country. [Prensa Libre](https://www.prensalibre.com/guatemala/comunitario/nuevo-formulario-para-viajar-a-estados-unidos-tres-puntos-clave-sobre-su-vigencia-presentacion-fisica-o-digital-y-que-pasa-si-no-lo-lleva/), [El Mañana](https://elmanana.com.mx/global/2026/10/30/turistas-deberan-cumplir-con-nuevo-requisito-si-van-a-volar-a-eu-183503.html), [RusTourismNews](https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/10/30/new-us-flight-rule-from-november-3-now-applies-to-all-passengers-and-crew/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-30: US measles cases reached 4,852 as of Oct 29. [Contagion Live](https://contagionlive.com/view/measles-update-october-30-2026), [CDC measles](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html)
- 2026-10-28: Costa Rica has 923 chikungunya cases this year, with clusters spreading in the Greater Metropolitan Area. CDC's Level 2 notice is still in place. [Global Risk Atlas](https://globalriskatlas.com/en/chikungunya-expansion-in-the-greater-metropolitan-area-of-costa-rica)
- 2026-10-20: ESCMID says PAHO rates measles risk in the Americas as very high. Guatemala and Mexico have most of the cases and deaths, though transmission there is reportedly declining. PAHO also says chikungunya is falling across the region overall, with exceptions in some Central American and Caribbean countries. [ESCMID Epi Alert](https://www.escmid.org/science-research/emerging-infections/epi-alert/), [MOSTI Care](https://www.mosticare.org/en/ressources/prevention/mosquito-borne-disease-latin-america-caribbean-travellers-from-europe)
- 2026-10-13: CDC's dengue page lists Cuba, Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras and Mexico among countries with dengue notices. Cuba met the high-transmission criteria on Oct 7. [CDC dengue areas](https://www.cdc.gov/dengue/areas-with-risk/index.html)
- I found no current cholera or Oropouche outbreak reports for the region.

## 4. Base rates
"New" North American notices I could identify, 2025-2026:
- About Oct to Nov 2025: Cuba chikungunya, Level 2, issued together with notices for Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Guangdong. The exact date is not confirmed, and the notice is no longer on the page. [Fox](https://www.fox5ny.com/news/cdc-warns-travelers-about-outbreak-untreatable-mosquito-disease-4-countries), [HealthDay](https://www.healthday.com/health-news/public-health/chikungunya-and-dengue-outbreak-in-cuba-has-left-33-dead-officials-say)
- 2025-12-23: Mexico Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever. The page does not label it "New."
- 2026-06-04: Canada Hepatitis A.
- 2026-06-25: Haiti diphtheria.
- About July 2026: Costa Rica chikungunya. It was raised to Level 2 on Jul 16. [Tico Times](https://ticotimes.net/2026/07/31/cdc-costa-rica-chikungunya-travel-notice-update)
- 2026-08-03: Nicaragua chikungunya, reported as a new notice. Sources disagree on whether it started at Level 1 or Level 2. [TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322990/20260804/cdc-issues-nicaragua-chikungunya-alert-suspended-vaccine-leaves-us-travelers-one-choice.htm)
- 2026-09-18: Costa Rica Hepatitis A.

What this adds up to:
- Every month from June to September 2026 had a new North American notice. I found none for October 2026 and could not establish January to May 2026.
- That is roughly 5 to 7 new North American notices a year, or about 0.4 to 0.6 a month. This is a rough count from limited data.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. They cover State Department advisories, Taiwan, oil, gold and other topics.
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on CDC THNs for North America.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Nov 3, 2026: the Ebola attestation requirement starts. It is not a North American THN.
- Possible triggers for a new notice in November:
  - Cuba's high-transmission dengue status, though that would more likely show up as an update to the Global Dengue notice.
  - Costa Rica's chikungunya spreading to new areas, which would more likely be an update to the existing notice.
  - Measles in Mexico and Guatemala, which is covered by the existing Global Measles notice.
  - A new outbreak, such as diphtheria, cholera or Oropouche, somewhere new.
- Updates to existing notices or multi-country notices may not count as "newly issued," so watch the "New" label on the THN page.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left and what is needed for Yes.** About one month, covering November 1 to 30, 2026. Yes requires the CDC Travel Health Notices page to show a notice newly issued in November for a North American country. That includes Canada, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. The background treats only "New" notices as qualifying, so an "Updated" label on an existing notice (Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Global Dengue) probably would not count, though there is some resolver ambiguity.

**(b) Status quo.** No new North American notice since September 18. With nothing changing, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate.** Over the last 12 months there were about 6 to 7 new North American notices, spread over 5 to 6 distinct months. That gives roughly 40 to 50% of months having at least one. The June to September 2026 cluster was unusually active, with a notice every month. Over a longer multi-year window it is more like 30 to 40% of months. I use about 40% as the base rate.

**(d) Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - Dengue is elevated: Mexico had 58,549 suspected cases through week 39, and Cuba is in the CDC's high-transmission category as of October 7.
  - The PAHO screwworm alert (October 16) reports human cases surging in Mexico and Central America.
  - Canada's Cuba and Nicaragua chikungunya notice (October 13) has no CDC counterpart yet.
  - Caribbean disease risk after hurricane season.
  - Many North American countries are candidates.
- **For No:**
  - October had no new North American notice, which suggests the summer cluster is fading.
  - November is past the peak arbovirus season.
  - CDC attention is on Ebola, with the Kenya notice on October 19 and the attestation order starting November 3.
  - Updates to existing notices likely do not count.
  - The CDC has historically not issued THNs for screwworm.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- **No:** The CDC refreshes the Global Dengue and Costa Rica chikungunya notices as "Updated", focuses on Ebola, and issues no new North American notice in November.
- **Yes:** The CDC issues a new chikungunya or Oropouche notice for Cuba, or a Level 1 notice for an outbreak such as measles in Mexico or post-storm disease in Jamaica or Haiti, in mid-November.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start at about 40%. I subtract a few points for the seasonal decline, the quiet October and CDC bandwidth going to Ebola. I add a little for the ambiguity over whether "Updated" notices count and for the active dengue and screwworm situation. Net, I land around 35%.

Probability: 35%

(a) The question resolves around December 1, 2026, about one month from now. Yes requires the CDC THN page to show a notice for a specific North American country with a "New" issue date in November 2026. An "Updated" status on an existing notice, such as Costa Rica chikungunya or Global Dengue, probably does not count, though a resolver could read it loosely.

(b) Status quo: no new North American notice has appeared since September 18. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: there were about 6 to 7 new North American notices in the last 12 months, falling in roughly 5 to 6 distinct months. That is about 40 to 50% of months. June through September 2026 each had one, and October had none. This suggests a crude rate of about 45%, with clustering in the arbovirus season.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - Mexico had 58,549 suspected dengue cases through week 39 (PAHO, 2026-10-23).
  - Canada issued its own chikungunya notice for Cuba and Nicaragua (2026-10-13), and the CDC has not matched it for Cuba.
  - PAHO issued a screwworm alert (2026-10-16) showing human cases surging in Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras.
  - Post-hurricane-season outbreaks in the Caribbean are possible.
  - The CDC's recent cadence for this region has been high.
- For No:
  - October produced no new North American notices.
  - The rainy season is ending in Central America.
  - CDC attention is focused on Ebola, including the attestation order effective November 3.
  - Screwworm has no THN precedent that I found.
  - Most likely changes would be updates rather than new notices.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: November passes with only updates to the Costa Rica, Nicaragua and Global Dengue notices, while CDC travel staff focus on Ebola in Kenya and the DRC.
- Yes: the CDC issues a Level 1 or 2 chikungunya notice for Cuba or Honduras, a dengue or Oropouche notice for another Caribbean country, or a Hepatitis A or measles notice for Mexico.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 45%. I adjust down slightly for three reasons: October's lull, the end of the seasonal peak, and the competing Ebola workload. I adjust up slightly for the small chance that a resolver counts an updated notice as newly issued. The net result is a modest move down, to about 40%.

Probability: 40%

(a) There is one month left, November 1 to 30, 2026, and the outcome will be known around December 1. For Yes, the CDC THN page must show a notice for a North American country with a November 2026 date and a "New" status. North America here includes Central America and the Caribbean. An "Updated" notice, such as the Global Dengue or Costa Rica chikungunya notices, most likely does not count. The question says "newly issued", and the background refers to the most recent "new notice".

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. October produced no new North American notice, and nothing is pending.

(c) Over the past 12 months, about 5 to 6 of 12 months had a new North American notice, which is roughly 45%. That figure is concentrated in June to September 2026, during the arbovirus season. January to May 2026 apparently had none. For a late-autumn month, the off-season months seem the better reference, so about 25 to 35%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Dengue is high in Mexico, with 58.5k suspected cases through week 39 (2026-10-23).
- Cuba is in the CDC's high dengue category (2026-10-07).
- Canada issued a Cuba and Nicaragua chikungunya notice on 2026-10-13 that the CDC has not matched.
- Screwworm is surging in Mexico and Central America (PAHO alert, 2026-10-16).
- The region has many countries that could receive a notice.

Evidence for No:
- October 2026 had no new North American notice.
- The THN page was last reviewed 2026-10-19, and CDC attention is on Ebola.
- The CDC has never issued a THN for screwworm.
- Dengue is covered by the global notice, so new dengue activity would most likely be an "Updated" status.
- Arbovirus season is ending.

(e) No scenario: the CDC updates the Global Dengue or Costa Rica notices but issues nothing new for the region, and its focus stays on the Ebola response. Yes scenario: the CDC issues a new Level 1 or 2 notice, for example chikungunya in Cuba again, Oropouche, measles in a specific country, or a post-hurricane outbreak in Haiti or Jamaica.

(f) I start at about 40% from the raw rolling rate and move down for three reasons. It is the off-season. October showed nothing new. Most likely updates would go into existing global notices or show as "Updated" rather than "New". I add a little for the breadth of eligible countries and the slight chance that a resolver counts an update. Net, I land at about 30%.

Probability: 30%

(a) About one month remains (Nov 1 to Nov 30, 2026), with resolution around Dec 1. For Yes, the CDC THN page must show a notice for a North American country, including Central America and the Caribbean, labeled "New" with a November 2026 date. Updates to existing notices, or additions to the Global Dengue or Global Measles notices, probably do not count.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. No new North American notice appeared between Sep 18 and Oct 31.

(c) Base rate: roughly 5 to 7 new North American notices per year, or about 0.4 to 0.6 per month. Under a Poisson model, the chance of at least one in a given month is about 33 to 45%. Notices clustered in 2026: four consecutive months (June to September) had at least one, but October had none.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Active outbreaks are ongoing. Costa Rica chikungunya was spreading in the metro area as of Oct 28.
  - Cuba met high dengue transmission criteria on Oct 7.
  - PAHO noted chikungunya exceptions in Central America and the Caribbean (Oct 20).
  - Measles risk in the Americas is rated very high.
  - The summer 2026 cadence was high.
- **For No:**
  - Most current threats are already covered by existing or global notices, so CDC would more likely update those than issue new ones (Costa Rica chikungunya Level 2, Global Dengue updated Oct 2, Global Measles).
  - October produced no new North American notice.
  - CDC attention is focused on Ebola (Kenya notice Oct 19, entry order Oct 22 to 30).

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** CDC updates the Costa Rica chikungunya notice and the Global Dengue list, but issues no "New" North American notice in November.
- **Yes:** A new outbreak, such as chikungunya in another Central American or Caribbean country, Oropouche, diphtheria, or a localized hepatitis A or measles cluster, prompts a new Level 1 or 2 notice dated in November.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 40%. I move down slightly because the status quo favors No, recent threats are already covered, and October was quiet. I move back up a little because outbreak activity is ongoing and a lenient resolver might count updates. The net result is about 35%.

Probability: 35%

(a) About 30 days remain: the November 2026 window runs to Nov 30, and the outcome is known around Dec 1. For Yes, the CDC THN page must show a notice for a North American country (including Central America and the Caribbean) newly issued in November 2026, most likely labeled "New." A lenient resolver might also count a new country-specific notice that is labeled "Updated," but that is uncertain.

(b) The status quo is No. As of Oct 31 there is no November notice, and none was issued for North America in October.
